seo.title: Pet Relocation Dubai to UK: Real Cost & Process (2026)
seo.meta_description: What it really costs to move your pet from Dubai to the UK — AED 12,000–18,000 for a dog, 4–8 weeks, no quarantine if done right. Transparent breakdown, no hidden fees.
seo.og_title: Dubai → UK pet relocation: the real cost, with no surprises

hero.h1: Pet relocation Dubai to UK: what it really costs
hero.subheading: Worried you're being overcharged — or that the UK's strict rules mean you'll get it wrong? Both fears are fair. Here's the real price, line by line, and the one timing mistake that costs people their pet's entry.

key_facts.answer: Relocating a pet from Dubai to the UK costs roughly AED 12,000–18,000 for a dog and AED 8,000–14,000 for a cat, takes about 4–8 weeks, and involves no quarantine — provided the paperwork is correct and (for dogs) the tapeworm treatment is given 1–5 days before arrival.

sections.heading: The cost, line by line
sections.intro: No “contact us for a quote” wall — here's where every dirham goes for a standard Dubai→UK move.
sections.note: Where you land in the range depends on your pet's size (airlines charge by crate volume, not just weight) and the airline. Get the paperwork wrong and UK customs delays can add AED 5,000+ — which is the whole reason the service fee exists.

sections.heading: The £-saving timing trap (read this)
sections.body: For dogs, the UK requires a tapeworm treatment 1–5 days before arrival — not earlier, not later. Too early and it's invalid; too late and your dog is refused entry or held. Cats don't need it. This single timing detail is the most common reason a Dubai→UK move goes wrong, and it's free to get right.

sections.heading: Why the price varies — and why cheapest isn't safest
paragraphs: Two pets, same route, can cost very differently. A small cat in a compact crate sits at the bottom of the range; a large dog whose crate measures big on volumetric weight sits at the top — sometimes AED 1,500+ more in air freight alone.

The other variable is who does the paperwork. The UK health certificate must come from an APHA-approved vet — most Dubai vets aren't on that list (DKC and British Vet Hospital are). Use the wrong vet and the certificate is rejected at the border. The cheapest quote that skips this check isn't cheap; it's a risk to your pet's entry.

sections.heading: Why owners trust a transparent price
sections.intro: Most UAE pet-relocation providers still hide pricing behind a 'get a quote' form. Here's how we're different.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to move a dog from Dubai to the UK?
faqs.a: Roughly AED 12,000–18,000 all-in for a standard route, depending on your dog's size (which sets the air-freight cost) and the airline. The full line-by-line breakdown is above — no hidden fees.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper for a cat?
faqs.a: Usually, yes — about AED 8,000–14,000, because cats travel in smaller crates and (unlike dogs) don't need the UK tapeworm treatment.

faqs.q: Will my pet have to go into quarantine in the UK?
faqs.a: No — the UK doesn't quarantine pets that arrive with correct paperwork. The risk isn't quarantine; it's a documentation error, which is exactly what we prevent.

faqs.q: Why can't I just use my normal Dubai vet?
faqs.a: The UK health certificate must come from an APHA-approved third-country vet. Most Dubai vets aren't on that list — DKC and British Vet Hospital are. We confirm approval before any appointment.

faqs.q: Can my XL Bully or Pit Bull come to the UK?
faqs.a: No. Pit Bull, XL Bully (banned since 1 February 2024), Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino and Fila Brasileiro are banned under the Dangerous Dogs Act. We verify your breed before booking.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee the arrival date?
faqs.a: No — and be wary of anyone who does. Airlines change cargo schedules, especially in the UAE summer heat. We give a realistic timeline and keep you updated, but never promise an exact arrival.
